content.description: Mirra Andreeva dominated her Toronto opener, winning the first six games and the last six games in a 54-minute rout of former World No. 1 Karolina Pliskova. In her first match since Wimbledon, Andreeva showed few signs of rust.

content.description: Ekaterina Alexandrova improved to 2-0 against No. 2 seed Mirra Andreeva with a straight-sets win in the Bad Homburg Open second round. The match was Andreeva's first since winning Roland Garros, and Alexandrova's first Top 5 win since Stuttgart 2025 (and 10th in total).

content.title: 'It bounced back!' Mirra Andreeva finds unlikely winner in Bad Homburg
content.description: Mirra Andreeva pulled off an absurd winner in the Bad Homburg Open second round against Ekaterina Alexandrova when she managed to load a defensive forehand dig with so much spin that it bounced back on her own side of the net.

content.title: Andreeva and Shnaider win Rome for second WTA 1000 title together
content.description: Mirra Andreeva and Diana Shnaider were dominant all week in Rome, and they continued to outclass their competition in Sunday's final, defeating Cristina Bucsa and Nicole Melichar-Martinez 6-3, 6-3 in 69 minutes to capture the title.

content.title: Gauff holds off Andreeva on fifth match point in Rome quarterfinal thriller
content.description: For the second year running, No. 3 seed Coco Gauff defeated No. 8 seed Mirra Andreeva in the Internazionali BNL d'Italia quarterfinals -- but this time, it was a 2-hour, 18-minute thriller which she needed five match points to close out as Andreeva attempted to come back from 5-1 down in the third set. content.title: Andreeva fends off Baptiste challenge to reach Madrid final
content.description: No. 9 seed Mirra Andreeva held off a late charge from 5-3 down in the second set by No. 30 seed Hailey Baptiste, saving three set points in the tiebreak, to reach her seventh career WTA final (and third at WTA 1000 level) at the Mutua Madrid Open.

content.title: Hot shot: Mirra Andreeva lands ‘majestic’ lob to save set point in Madrid
content.description: How's this for clutch touch? Down double set point, having already missed a match point, Mirra Andreeva patiently soaked up a barrage of groundstrokes from Hailey Baptiste -- and then, drawing her opponent to net, lofted a "majestic" lob winner over her head.

content.title: Andreeva saves three set points vs. Fernandez; into first Madrid semifinal
content.description: No. 9 seed Mirra Andreeva came from 4-1 down in the first set, saving three set points, to defeat No. 24 seed Leylah Fernandez in the Mutua Madrid Open quarterfinals. Andreeva advanced to her fourth semifinal at WTA 1000 level or above, and improved to 2-1 overall against Fernandez.

content.title: Andreeva holds off Bondar in 2:53 Madrid marathon to make quarters
content.description: No. 9 seed Mirra Andreeva reached the Mutua Madrid Open quarterfinals for a third successive year with a 2-hour, 53-minute defeat of Anna Bondar. Andreeva led 5-1 in the third set, and held her first match point at 5-3, but had to recover after Bondar won five straight games to win the deciding tiebreak. The result reversed Bondar's win in their only previous meeting, in the 2023 Lausanne second round.

content.title: From a break down in both sets, Andreeva tops Galfi to make Madrid last 16
content.description: No. 9 seed Mirra Andreeva booked her place in a fourth successive last-16 appearance at the Mutua Madrid Open with a straight-sets defeat of qualifier Dalma Galfi.

content.title: Andreeva beats Udvardy to reach Madrid third round
content.description: Ninth-seeded Mirra Andreeva scored a straight-sets victory over Panna Udvardy to reach the third round of the Mutua Madrid Open. She will next face qualifier Dalma Galfi.

content.title: Returning to the site of her breakthrough, Andreeva reflects on her rise
Andreeva comes from a set down to knock out Swiatek in Stuttgart quarterfinals
content.description: Mirra Andreeva dropped the opening set to Iga Swiatek but came back to score a 3-6, 6-4, 6-3 win in a 2-hour, 36-minute thriller on Friday against the two-time Stuttgart champ to book her spot in the semifinals. Andreeva improved to 3-1 overall against Swiatek in their first clay-court meeting.

content.title: Andreeva holds off Parks in Stuttgart, extends winning streak to six
content.description: No. 6 seed Mirra Andreeva improved to 2-0 against qualifier Alycia Parks with a straight-sets win in the Porsche Tennis Grand Prix second round. The Linz champion extended her winning streak to six and advanced to her fifth quarterfinal of 2026, where she will face former World No. 1 Iga Swiatek.

content.title: Andreeva overturns 4-1 third-set deficit to dethrone Ostapenko in Stuttgart
content.description: No. 6 seed Mirra Andreeva dethroned defending champion Jelena Ostapenko in the Porsche Tennis Grand Prix first round, winning the last five straight games from 4-1 down in the third set.

content.title: Champions Reel: How Mirra Andreeva won Linz 2026
content.description: No. 1 seed Mirra Andreeva captured her fifth career WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz title, second on clay, fourth at WTA 500 level or above and second of 2026 at the Upper Austria Ladies Linz. Andreeva defeated Anastasia Potapova, the first Austrian player to reach the tournament final, in the title match.

content.title: Andreeva wins second title of season in Linz
content.description: Top-seeded Mirra Andreeva rallied from a set down to defeat Austria’s Anastasia Potapova in three sets and win the Upper Austria Ladies Linz title on Sunday. It is her second singles title of the season and the fifth of her career.

content.title: Andreeva reaches second final of the season in Linz
content.description: Top seed Mirra Andreeva advanced to the final of the Upper Austria Ladies Linz with a 6-4, 6-1 win over Romania’s Elena-Gabriela Ruse. She will face Anastasia Potapova or qualifier Donna Vekic in Sunday’s final.

content.title: Andreeva overcomes Cirstea to reach Linz semifinals
content.description: Top seed Mirra Andreeva outlasted Sorana Cirstea in three sets to reach the semifinals of the Upper Austria Ladies Linz. She will face unseeded Elena-Gabriela Ruse for a spot in the final.

content.title: Andreeva bests Stephens to get her clay season underway in Linz
content.description: Mirra Andreeva defeated Sloane Stephens 6-4, 6-2 in 1 hour and 21 minutes on Wednesday in her first match on clay this season to book her spot in the Linz quarterfinals.

content.title: Mboko tops Andreeva in Miami three-setter; into fourth WTA 1000 quarterfinal
content.description: No. 10 seed Victoria Mboko took a 2-1 lead in her rivalry with No. 8 seed Mirra Andreeva with a three-set victory in the Miami Open quarterfinals. Mboko advanced to her fourth career WTA 1000 quarterfinal.

content.title: From 5-0 down, Andreeva/Mboko defeat Perez/Schuurs in Miami
content.description: Mirra Andreeva and Victoria Mboko upset No. 8 seeds Ellen Perez and Demi Schuurs in the Miami Open first round, coming from 5-0 down to win the first set (saving seven set points along the way).

content.title: Threading the needle! Mirra Andreeva pulls off pinpoint pass in Miami
content.description: Mirra Andreeva had almost no room to work with after Marie Bouzkova tracked down her drop shot in the Miami Open third round, but managed to squeeze a laser-like pass down the line for the winner.

content.title: Andreeva saves two set points, out-foxes Bouzkova to make Miami last 16
content.description: No. 8 seed Mirra Andreeva saved two set points serving down 5-4 in the first set, then came from 2-0 down in the second set to defeat No. 32 seed Marie Bouzkova in the Miami Open third round. Andreeva improved to 4-0 against Bouzkova (and 8-0 in sets).

content.title: Andreeva outlasts Kessler in late-night battle to survive and advance in Miami
content.description: Mirra Andreeva had to fight off a McCartney Kessler upset bid into the early hours of Friday morning in Miami, but ultimately got the job done with a 6-1, 6-7 (3), 6-1 victory in just under two hours to reach the third round.

content.title: Andreeva/Mboko save two match points, edge Baptiste/Ostapenko in Indian Wells
content.description: Mirra Andreeva and Victoria Mboko saved three set points in the first set and two match points in the match tiebreak to defeat wild cards Hailey Baptiste and Jelena Ostapenko in the BNP Paribas Open second round.

content.title: Siniakova upsets defending champion Andreeva in Indian Wells thriller
content.description: Katerina Siniakova advanced to her first Indian Wells fourth round and seventh career Round of 16 at a WTA 1000, upsetting reigning champion Mirra Andreeva 4-6, 7-6 (5), 6-3. In a tense battle that featured 42 break point opportunities, Siniakova saved 19 of the 26 she faced.

content.title: Andreeva blanks Sierra in Indian Wells for 100th WTA Tour win
content.description: Mirra Andreeva couldn't be stopped in her second-round match against Solana Sierra, winning 6-0, 6-0 in 50 minutes to open her Indian Wells title defense and advance to the third round. In the process, she collected WTA win No. 100.

content.title: Teenage stars Mboko, Andreeva upset Australian Open champs Mertens, Zhang at Indian Wells
content.description: Top 10 singles players and teenage stars Mirra Andreeva and Victoria Mboko teamed up at the last minute to play doubles at Indian Wells, upsetting Australian Open champs Elise Mertens and Shuai Zhang 6-4, 4-6, [10-8] in the first round of the BNP Paribas Open.

content.title: Anisimova triumphs over Andreeva in third-set tiebreak to make Dubai semis
content.description: No. 2 seed Amanda Anisimova ended Mirra Andreeva's Dubai Duty Free Tennis Championships defense in the quarterfinals, holding off a late charge by the No. 5 seed to win a third-set tiebreak. Anisimova improved to 2-0 overall against Andreeva.

content.title: 'Genius!' Andreeva foils Anisimova with lob and drop shot combo in Dubai
content.description: Mirra Andreeva seemed to have no hope of winning this rally in the Dubai Duty Free Tennis Championships quarterfinals as Amanda Anisimova shaped up to put away a backhand sitter. But Andreeva anticipated Anisimova's down-the-line direction and turned the point on its head, lofting a lob over the American's head before finishing with a deft drop shot.

content.title: Andreeva holds off Cristian to open belated Dubai title defense
content.description: No. 5 seed Mirra Andreeva opened her Dubai Duty Free Tennis Championships title defense -- after receiving a first-round bye and second-round walkover -- with a tight two-set win over Jaqueline Cristian in the third round.

content.title: From match point down, Mboko gains first win over Andreeva in Doha
content.description: No. 10 seed Victoria Mboko levelled her head-to-head with No. 5 seed Mirra Andreeva at 1-1 after edging a three-set win from match point down in an all-teenage Qatar TotalEnergies Open third round. Mboko notched her third career Top 10 win and advanced to her second WTA 1000 quarterfinal.

content.title: Andreeva battles past Linette to reach Doha third round for the first time
content.description: Mirra Andreeva saved five set points to send the opener to a tiebreak in her second-round match against Magda Linette. Once there, she blanked Linette in the breaker, then dominated the second set to advance to the third round in Doha for the first time.

content.title: Full match replay: How Andreeva finally stopped Mboko in the 2026 Adelaide final
Champions Reel: How Mirra Andreeva won Adelaide 2026
content.description: No. 3 seed Mirra Andreeva won her fifth career WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz title, third on hard courts and first since Indian Wells 2025 at the Adelaide International 2026 without dropping a set. Andreeva, 18, defeated two fellow teenagers -- 19-year-olds Maya Joint and, in the final, Victoria Mboko -- as well as former doubles partner Diana Shnaider en route to the trophy.

content.title: Andreeva bests Mboko in battle of the teens to capture fourth career title
content.description: Mirra Andreeva was dominant all week in Adelaide, and that high level continued in the final, as she used a run of nine straight games between the first and second sets to defeat Victoria Mboko 6-3, 6-1 to earn her first WTA 500 title.

content.title: Andreeva hits top form to best Shnaider in Adelaide; into fifth WTA final
content.description: No. 3 seed Mirra Andreeva delivered some dazzling tennis to defeat former doubles partner and No. 9 seed Diana Shnaider in the Adelaide International semifinals, advancing to her fifth career final and first since winning Indian Wells last March.

content.title: Four incredible steals by Mirra Andreeva in the Adelaide semifinals
content.description: A forehand down the line from way outside the tramlines? A pinpoint lob followed by a brilliant backhand down the line? A reflexed lob off a smash? Exquisite touch at net? Mirra Andreeva did it all against Diana Shnaider in the Adelaide International semifinals.

content.title: Andreeva drops just two games against Joint to make Adelaide semis
content.description: No. 3 seed Mirra Andreeva, 18, raced past Maya Joint, 19, in just 67 minutes to reach the Adelaide International semifinals. The all-teenage clash was the pair's first pro meeting; Andreeva won their only junior encounter in 2022.

content.title: Andreeva wins 11 of the last 12 games to take out Bouzkova in Adelaide
content.description: No. 3 seed Mirra Andreeva reached her second quarterfinal of 2026 with a straight-sets win over lucky loser Marie Bouzkova in the Adelaide International second round. Andreeva improved to 3-0 overall against Bouzkova.

content.title: Andreeva saves two match points, wins sixth edition of rivalry vs. Noskova
content.description: No. 6 seed Mirra Andreeva improved to 4-2 against No. 9 seed Linda Noskova (and 2-1 in Brisbane) after saving two match points to triumph in their Brisbane International third-round contest.

content.title: Andreeva resets from a set down to quell Gadecki in Brisbane second round
content.description: No. 6 seed Mirra Andreeva bounced back from a set down to defeat qualifier Olivia Gadecki in the Brisbane International second round, improving to 2-0 overall against the Australian.

Relive the moment: Andreeva stuns Sabalenka to win Indian Wells
content.description: Mirra Andreeva, then 17, came from behind to beat World No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka 2-6, 6-4, 6-3 in the BNP Paribas Open final. It was Andreeva's second consecutive WTA 1000 title after winning Dubai.

content.description: Mirra Andreeva took care of business Monday in Beijing, handling the missiles coming off the racket of Jessica Bouzas Maneiro to secure a 6-4, 6-1 victory in 1 hour and 32 minutes and advance to the fourth round of the China Open.

content.title: Anisimova rallies in Miami to end Andreeva's 13-match winning streak
content.description: No. 17 seed Amanda Anisimova toppled No. 11 seed Mirra Andreeva 7-6(5), 2-6, 6-3 in the third round of the Miami Open on Sunday night, ending the teen's hopes of completing the Sunshine Double.

content.title: In Miami debut, Mirra Andreeva posts 13th straight tour-level win
content.description: In her first-ever match at the Miami Open, No. 11 seed Mirra Andreeva collected her 20th tour-level win of the year (and 13th straight) with a 6-0, 6-2 dismissal of Veronika Kudermetova on Friday.

content.title: Champions Reel: How Mirra Andreeva won Indian Wells 2025
content.description: No. 9 seed Mirra Andreeva captured her third Hologic WTA Tour title, and second at WTA 1000 level in a row, at the 2025 BNP Paribas Open. Andreeva, 17, extended her winning streak to 12 following her title run in Dubai. She became the youngest player to win back-to-back WTA 1000/Tier I trophies since Martina Hingis in 1997, and the youngest player to defeat the World No. 1 and World No. 2 in the same tournament since Tracy Austin in 1979.
